brief: Hedge funds cut risk sharply this week as AI, semiconductor and other high-growth names sold off hard. GS Prime data shows net deleveraging milder than during the Iran-war selloff, while gross leverage ratios rose as fund equity fell faster than exposure. Info Tech was the most net-sold global sector, AI-stock selling by hedge funds hit a five-year extreme on a trailing 20-day basis, and hedge fund exposure to semis fell to single digits, while Mag7 net length still sits near cycle-high percentiles. The Nasdaq 100's forward P/E dropped to 18.4x, its lowest since 2020. Thursday brought one of Mag7's biggest down moves in years, and dealers pulled back, draining E-mini liquidity. S&P buyback demand is running near $5bn a day with 90% of corporates in their open window, and order volumes accelerated into the back half of the week on post-election momentum and earnings. Bloomberg reports unverified allegations against Jensen Huang. The note says it does not know what happened. If true, the market would ask what else he could have misled people about. Nvidia is barely up year-to-date with RSI at Liberation Day lows, though Berkshire has outperformed Nvidia by about 15 percentage points over the past year.
